From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-20T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: 15-20% error rate and 3x latency for /v1/generate

Priya / Marissa —

Quick diagnostic from the serving layer: the dedicated GPU pool for QuickCard hit a headroom threshold at ~07:38 PDT. Observations:
- Token-per-request increased ~2.8x due to longer responses; KV-cache eviction rates spiked causing higher compute per request.
- A small subset of clients (3 internal QuickCard routes) account for ~60% of the added load.
- Autoscale attempts were limited by reserved cap — the pool cannot exceed the committed capacity without explicit burst authorization.

Short-term mitigations we can apply now (ordered by speed):
1) Route non-critical traffic to the hosted fallback model (gpt-medium-q8) — reduces load on reserved GPUs immediately.
2) Push a conservative prefix-caching policy for the hot routes (cuts repeated compute).
3) Reduce default max_tokens / beam settings for QuickCard temporarily (they agreed to roll this back if needed).

I attached a snapshot of the GPU queue depth and utilization for 07:00-09:00. If we need sustained relief we'll require an emergency burst authorization from capacity control (and an exec nod if we plan to extend beyond 2 hours).

Attachment: pool_metrics_20280320.png

-David
David Kim
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priya —

Thank you for the quick response. We are willing to accept routing to the hosted fallback for non-critical flows, but this is still a customer-impacting outage and we need an answer on:
1) Whether this qualifies as an SLA breach under our reserved contract.
2) What credits we will get and how they will be calculated.
3) When (ETA) we can expect a return to normal for our main reserved pool without degrading quality.

We require a CTO-level call if the root cause persists beyond 2 hours; please escalate accordingly. I'll prepare an incident summary and share logs (attached).

Regards,
Maria

Team — raising to leadership as QuickCard remains at elevated error/latency levels after initial mitigations. Summary: 
- Impact: P95 latency 2.9x baseline / 12% 5xx across peak window. QuickCard is an enterprise customer on a reserved capacity plan (DEAL-3421).
- Cause: sudden spike in token-per-request combined with KV-cache pressure; dedicated pool headroom exhausted.
- Actions taken: routed non-critical traffic to hosted fallback; applied prefix caching for hot routes; engaged SRE for deeper remediation. Metrics and traces attached.
- Ask (immediate):
  1) Emergency burst authorization for +25% GPU capacity for 3 hours (will require approval from capacity control and execs).
  2) Approval to temporarily allow cross-region spillover (US -> EU) for QuickCard while we stabilize.
  3) Pre-approve a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of committed capacity if SLA is adjudicated as breached (we should be ready to propose numbers to Maria).

If we don't get burst authorization within 30 minutes we risk continued customer degradation and escalation to their CTO (they've requested a CTO-level call at 2 hours). Please respond with approvals or alternative mitigations.
